answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 64x48 rectangle (width 64 on every row) filled with mottled brown earth texture. Grass tufts (yellow seed heads, green shoots) and a few grey and reddish pebbles are scattered across the surface at rows 3-15, 18-31, 33-47. There is no front face, no edge line, no eave shadow and no standing volume. The column scans show only texture variation, with no band structure. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows 5 visible tones per tile, above the grass reference (3) and below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 1%, so there are no large flat fills, and the dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so there is no sticker outline. The soil is mottled brown with a few dark crack and speckle marks, and the yellow grass tufts have a few highlight and dark pixels. Only 15 distinct colours are used, and the soil ramp is about 4 steps against the references' richer 5-6. The tufts are small and sparse, drawn mostly as 2-3 tone clusters, so the shading is thinner than Beodeul's per-clump multi-green treatment. The soil grain is fairly uniform and repeats, and it lacks per-clump or per-stone shading. It is clean and acceptable but a little lighter than the references, so it falls short of the bar when in doubt.
